2024.DI6.5.t: Accessible Taxis and Cars for Hire Services
2024.DI6.5.s:
On March 27th, we received an information request to provide a presentation by Spinal Cord Injury Ontario (SCIO) on the topic of Accessible Taxis and Vehicle for Hire Services.

Upon research conducted by the SCIO community, we have learned that finding a wheelchair accessible Taxi or Vehicle for Hire Service has become increasingly difficult in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) since the pandemic. People with disabilities are waiting record times to get access to transportation that their fellow residents without disabilities can access in under ten minutes.

It is for this reason that we believe Spinal Cord Injury Ontario should have the opportunity to speak at the upcoming Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee. They are a provincial organization that specialize in serving people with spinal cord injuries and other disabilities. As such, they regularly hear the lived experience perspective from across Ontario and are best equipped to bring the needs of the disability community to City Councilors.

Stories from SCIO’s community have led to recent media stories, where accessible Taxi and Vehicle for Hire Service end users were interviewed on television, highlighting the barriers that are in place.

Moreover, people with disabilities have started a change.org petition, bringing attention to this matter that is impacting thousands of lives on a daily basis, leaving them stranded or incurring fees …
2024.DI6.5.r:
Dana Francoz and Luke Anderson, Members, Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee jointly recommend that the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee:

1. Invite Spinal Cord Injury Ontario to do a presentation on the topic of Accessible Taxis and Vehicle for Hire Services at Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee’s meeting on June 24, 2024.

2024.DI8.4.t: Accessibility Protection Zones Around Construction Projects
2024.DI8.4.s:
Please see the below letter that I am submitting to Toronto Accessibility Access Committee on behalf of Corina McCoy:

“My name is Corina McCoy and I have a newly acquired disability and have quickly become aware that construction projects limit my access to the city as well as creating unsafe situations for me as I move throughout it. In trying to figure out what to do to change this situation I came across the Toronto Accessibility Access Committee (TAAC). Therefore, I am writing to you to ask that you request City Staff to create an Accessibility Access Protection Zone Policy. Some further details are below.

I have had the chance to watch recordings of some of your meetings and see that TAAC has had several presentations about accessibility in construction zones from City Staffers, however I have noticed the following.

1. There are great Ideas for improved access, but implementation is based on “culture change” and “education of stakeholders”. In other words, hope is a strategy that there will be improvements.

2. There are no timeframes, goals, or metrics, KPIs, OKRs or stated desired outcomes.

3. There are no paths to change, processes, guidelines, or implementation plans.…

2024.DI10.6.s:
The City of Toronto is developing a third Toronto Seniors Strategy to better support aging in place, particularly for seniors who are Indigenous, Black, and who belong to equity-deserving groups.

The City of Toronto will be implementing a community consultation process to enhance the City’s understanding of the priorities of seniors and older adults in Toronto. These consultations will be a key input into the development of the next Toronto Seniors Strategy.

The experiences of seniors with disabilities must be included in this strategy, and people with disabilities should be a specific priority group for consultations.

The strategy should be designed with an accessibility lens.
